Abstract

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga _Chlamydomonas nivalis_ by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization (LC–APCI-MS). Samples were extracted with methanol and analyzed by LC separation followed by APCI-MS detection in positive ion mode.  Characteristic mass spectral features, including protonated molecular ions and fragmentation patterns, were used to identify two novel astaxanthin diglucoside diesters.  The structures of these compounds were elucidated based on their mass and fragmentation data, along with comparison with published spectra of known astaxanthin glycosides. This methodology provides a sensitive and specific tool for the identification and characterization of astaxanthin glycoside esters in natural sources, contributing to a better understanding of the carotenoid profile of _Chlamydomonas nivalis_ and its role in snow algal pigmentation.

## Primary Resistance to Single and Multiple Drugs in Leprosy: A Mouse Footpad Study

Skin biopsy homogenates obtained from three cases of lepromatous leprosy with no prior history of antileprosy treatment were tested in the mouse footpad for the sensitivity of _Mycobacterium leprae_ to multiple drugs.  We investigated the in vivo susceptibility of _M. leprae_ isolates to individual first-line antileprosy drugs (dapsone, rifampicin, clofazimine) and their combinations, comparing the bacterial load and lesion size in infected footpads after eight weeks. Our findings revealed variable responses to individual drugs, with one isolate exhibiting a significantly higher bacterial load and larger lesion size compared to the others when treated with dapsone alone.  Furthermore, treatment with combinations of dapsone and rifampicin, or all three first-line drugs,  demonstrated reduced bacterial burden and lesion size across all isolates, suggesting potential synergistic effects. These results highlight the importance of individual drug susceptibility testing, even in treatment-naive leprosy patients, and emphasize the crucial role of multidrug therapy in achieving effective bacterial control.  This study provides preliminary evidence for potential primary drug resistance in leprosy, warranting further investigation and careful consideration of personalized treatment strategies.

generations.raw_text: As a member of the testis-specific serine/threonine protein kinase (TSSK) family, Tssk4 is exclusively expressed in the testis and plays an essential role in male fertility. We previously reported that Tssk4 is highly enriched in the flagella of mature spermatozoa and is involved in sperm motility.  This study investigates the functional relevance of Tssk4 by identifying its potential downstream targets. Through an unbiased phosphoproteomic approach, we identified Odf2, a component of the outer dense fibers essential for sperm flagellar structural integrity, as a direct phosphorylation target of Tssk4. We confirmed this interaction in vitro and in vivo, demonstrating that Tssk4 phosphorylates Odf2 specifically at Serine-76.  Furthermore, mutating Ser-76 to Alanine in Odf2 significantly impaired sperm motility, suggesting a critical role for this phosphorylation site in male fertility. These findings highlight a novel function for Tssk4 in regulating sperm function through Odf2 phosphorylation and provide further insights into the complex molecular mechanisms underlying male fertility.

## Collision Synthesis of Unique Carbon Nanomaterials Inspired by the Allende Meteorite

A simple shock event approach inspired by the Allende meteorite to produce sophisticated carbon nanomaterials is reported. It is demonstrated that unique carbon nanostructures, including carbon nanotubes, carbon onions, and new carbon nanorings are synthesized through controlled collisions of graphite targets under high-pressure conditions.  The resulting nanomaterials exhibit distinct morphologies and size distributions, directly correlated with the parameters of the collision event. Characterization techniques, such as Raman spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction, reveal the structural features and graphitic nature of the synthesized nanomaterials. This innovative method offers a novel and sustainable pathway for producing diverse carbon nanostructures with potential applications in areas like nanoelectronics, catalysis, and energy storage. The findings provide insights into the potential role of high-energy cosmic events in the formation of complex carbon nanomaterials in extraterrestrial environments.
